output.summary: A perennial native throughout Europe and into western Siberia, common soapwort has sweet-scented pink or sometimes white flowers that open in the evening and smell stronger at night. Boiled leaves or roots produce a lathery cleaning liquid. Despite toxic potential, it is used commercially in tahini and brewing, while the root is often added when making halva in the Middle East.
